test_title: SSC Selection Post HSC Level Official Paper (Held on: 2 Aug 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution:
Here the correct answer is** "were immense gaps".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct answer for **blank number 3** is** "were immense gaps."**
 
• The use of** "were"** is appropriate as it agrees with the plural subject **"gaps" **in the sentence.** **
 
• **"Gaps" **is the appropriate noun to use in this context as it implies that there were empty spaces on the shelves where products should have been.
 
• The phrase** "there were immense gaps"** implies that there were significant shortages of products on the shelves.
 
• The use of the past tense** "were"** is also appropriate as it reflects the state of the shop at the time that the speaker is describing, rather than a current or ongoing state.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

Correct Paragraph:__ *My worries were increasing. The boy at the shop was becoming more clamorous. My sales were poor, as the railways (1) __were admitting__* *more peddlers on the platforms. My cash receipts were going down and my credit sales alone (2) __flourished__. The wholesale merchants who supplied me with goods stopped credit to me. The boy's method of account-keeping was so chaotic that I did not know whether I was moving forward or backward. He produced cash from the counter in a haphazard manner, and there **(3) **__**were immense gaps**__* *on the shelves all over the shop. The boy was probably pocketing money and eating off the stuff. With my credit at the wholesalers' gone, the public complained that nothing one wanted was ever available. Suddenly, the railways gave me notice to quit. I (4) ______ the old stationmaster and porter, but they could do nothing; the order had come from (5) ______. The shop was given to a new contractor.*
